about: The evangelium of the formulary “8th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus addressed His disciples with this parable: There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and the steward was reported to him as having squandered his goods. So he summoned him and said to him: What is this that I hear of you? Give an account of your stewardship, since you can no longer be steward. And the steward said to himself: What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my stewardship? To dig I am not strong enough; to beg I am ashamed. I know what I will do, so that, once I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses. So he called in his master’s debtors one by one, and said to the first: How much do you owe my master? He replied: A hundred jars of oil. And he told him: Take your note; sit down at once and write fifty. Next he said to another: And you, how much do you owe? He said: A hundred cors of wheat. He told him: Take your bond and write eighty. And the master commended the unjust steward because he had acted wisely; for the children of this world are wiser than the children of light in their own generation. And I say to you, make yourselves friends by means of the unjust mammon, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the everlasting dwellings.
